title: Key/value record dump/parse round trip
description: Implement dump_record(record) and parse_record(text), a one-line serialization for dict[str, str]. dump_record joins entries as 'key=value' pairs separated by ';', with entries sorted by their raw (unescaped) key. Inside keys and values, '%' is escaped as '%25', '=' as '%3D', ';' as '%3B' (uppercase hex, applied to '%' first). Empty dict dumps to ''. parse_record reverses it: '' parses to {}, entries are split on ';', each entry must contain '=', key and value are split on the first '=' and then unescaped. Unescaping accepts only '%' followed by two uppercase hex digits from the set 0-9A-F; any other '%' usage (lone '%', one digit, lowercase hex, non-hex digits) raises ValueError. A duplicate key (after unescaping) raises ValueError. record must be a dict with str keys and str values (else TypeError); text must be a str (else TypeError). Empty keys and empty values are allowed.
invariants: Round trip: parse_record(dump_record(record)) == record for every dict with str keys and str values, including keys/values containing '=', ';', '%', spaces, or empty strings.
dump_record output is deterministic: entries sorted by raw key, escapes uppercase ('%3B', not '%3b').
Escaping order matters: '%' is escaped first, so a literal '%3B' in the input survives the round trip unchanged.
Split on the FIRST '=' only: an escaped '=' never acts as the separator, and the separator is the first raw '='.
parse_record rejects an entry with no '=', a lone or malformed '%' escape, lowercase hex escapes, and duplicate keys: all ValueError.
